subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Gambler's Fallacy
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Gambler's Fallacy usable.

hook.text: A roulette wheel lands red five times. Gamblers pile onto black. The odds haven't changed at all.

buildup.text: The gambler's fallacy: believing past random events change the probability of future independent events.

discovery.text: Each spin is independent. The wheel has no memory. Red five times doesn't make black more likely.

twist.text: In 1913 at Monte Carlo, black came up 26 times in a row. Millions were lost betting on red.

climax.text: Our brains expect patterns in randomness. We see streaks as signals—but coins don't keep score.

quiz.question: What is the gambler's fallacy?
options: Believing past random events affect future probabilities
